stories.title: Domenicali Confirms Radical 2027 Calendar — 24 Races, 10 Sprints, Monaco Gets a Sprint

x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text:
Domenicali just confirmed the 2027 F1 calendar: 24 races + 10 sprints.

Monaco is getting a sprint race for the first time ever.

The full schedule drops "in the autumn." Middle East contingency plans are in place.

#F1 #Formula1

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text:
Ten sprint races in 2027. Ten.

Monaco Sprint is going to be either incredible or carnage. Maybe both.

Love it or hate it — F1 is going all-in on the format. #F1 #Formula1

facebook.long_form:
Window: 10:00 AM ET

Formula 1's 2027 season is going to look very different — and Stefano Domenicali confirmed it today.

The 2027 F1 calendar will feature 24 grand prix and 10 sprint races. Ten. That's double the current sprint count, and it includes a sprint race at Monaco — something previously considered unthinkable at the street circuit where there's barely room to overtake, let alone run a standalone sprint format.

Domenicali said the push is driven by a desire to bring "intensity" to the schedule. The full calendar is expected to be presented in the autumn. For the season opener, Bahrain and Saudi Arabia remain the target in mid-March, though Middle East contingency plans are in place given the ongoing regional conflict.

2026 already saw two rounds cancelled (Bahrain and Saudi Arabia) due to the situation, leaving a 22-race calendar. The plan for 2027 is to restore full strength — and go further.

x_posts.text:
Eight wins. Six poles. Twelve podiums in 14 races.

Kimi Antonelli at 20 years old is running away with the 2026 F1 title.

Baku is next. Nine rounds until it's official. #F1 #MercedesAMGF1

facebook.long_form:
Window: 8:00 AM ET

The numbers tell the story for Kimi Antonelli.

After 14 rounds of the 2026 Formula 1 season, the 20-year-old Mercedes driver leads the Drivers' Championship with 292 points — 81 clear of his own teammate, George Russell. He has eight wins, six pole positions, and 12 podiums in 14 races. At this point in the season, the question isn't whether he'll win the title. The question is when.

The math: 233 points remain across nine rounds (including one sprint). The earliest Antonelli can mathematically clinch is Singapore. The next race is Baku on Saturday, September 26 — moved from its usual Sunday slot to avoid a clash with Azerbaijan Remembrance Day, making it the first F1 race in history to run on a Saturday at this circuit.

He is the story of 2026.

stories.title: Williams' "Almost Entirely New Car" for Baku — But Sainz Warns Not to Expect Magic

x_posts.label: Post 3-1
x_posts.text:
Williams' Baku upgrade is what James Vowles called "almost an entirely new car."

Alex Albon says it won't fix their season.

Carlos Sainz says don't expect miracles.

Williams sits 9th with 11 points — none since Monaco in June. #F1

x_posts.label: Post 3-2
x_posts.text:
Williams skipped the Barcelona January shakedown due to production delays.

That decision cost them the start of the 2026 regulation cycle.

Now they're at Baku with "almost an entirely new car" trying to salvage the season. #F1

facebook.long_form:
Window: 12:00 PM ET

Williams are banking everything on Baku — and even their own drivers aren't sure it'll pay off.

Team principal James Vowles has been building anticipation for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix upgrade all season, at one point describing the package as "almost an entirely new car." It's Williams' biggest single development push of 2026, and it arrives at a circuit — the long-power-sensitive Baku streets — that at least gives them a fighting chance.

The catch: neither Alex Albon nor Carlos Sainz has been willing to endorse the hype. Albon has admitted the upgrade "won't fix" their 2026 season. Sainz has issued a "stark warning" not to expect a rescue package.

The backstory matters here. Williams missed the January Barcelona shakedown due to production delays — a decision that cost them crucial development time at the start of the new 2026 regulation cycle. The team that won multiple podiums in 2025 now sits ninth in the Constructors' Championship with 11 points, none since Monaco in June.

Baku is their biggest shot. They're just not promising anything.

stories.title: Ferrari Under Siege — McLaren Now Just 52 Points Back in Constructors'

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text:
McLaren are just 52 points behind Ferrari in the Constructors'.

That gap was 59 after the Italian GP. It's closing fast.

Nine rounds left. Ferrari's No. 2 spot is under real threat. #F1 #ScuderiaFerrari

facebook.long_form:
Window: 12:00 PM ET

Ferrari's grip on second place in the Constructors' Championship is loosening.

After the Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid, McLaren has pulled to within 52 points of Ferrari in the standings. That gap was 59 points after the Italian Grand Prix — meaning McLaren are closing at roughly 7 points per race. With nine rounds remaining, that trajectory is alarming for Maranello.

Mercedes is long gone in first place with 503 points — 145 clear of Ferrari. But the battle for second place has real stakes: it represents prestige, prize money, and arguably the team's ability to recruit and retain talent heading into 2027.

Ferrari needs a strong Baku. McLaren needs more of the same. Either way, this fight is far from over.

stories.title: Hamilton's Season Is About Pride Now — Baku Could Deliver

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:
Lewis Hamilton is 101 points back with 9 races left. The 2026 title is gone.

But Baku suits Ferrari's power-circuit strengths — and Hamilton has won here before.

Sometimes pride is the prize. #F1 #ScuderiaFerrari

facebook.long_form:
Window: 5:00 PM ET

Lewis Hamilton is 101 points behind Kimi Antonelli in the Drivers' Championship with nine races left.

That's not a gap you come back from at this stage of the season. Hamilton's 2026 title defense — his first season at Ferrari — has fallen short of the dream. His championship is, for all realistic purposes, over.

But Formula 1 doesn't stop, and Baku is next.

The Azerbaijan Grand Prix circuit is a power-track dream: long straights, high speeds, and the kind of racing that suits Ferrari's characteristics. Hamilton has won on the streets of Baku before. The race is on Saturday, September 26, and while he can't win the championship, he can win the race.

Sometimes the goal shifts from lifting a trophy to winning your own internal battle. Baku is that kind of moment for Hamilton in 2026.
